title_candidates: Inspect suspicious Bluesky replies without jumping to conclusions
summary: Simon Willison's new browser checker exposes the patterns behind suspicious replies. Try it in ten minutes, but treat its flags as leads, not proof of AI authorship.

primary_source.title: Tool: Bluesky reply bot checker
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Released September 27, built with Claude Opus 5.5 according to author.
Examines timing, posting mix and reply patterns on public Bluesky profiles.

supporting_sources.title: Bluesky reply bot checker
key_facts: Live browser test completed September 29 without sign-in, key, payment or installation using author's public handle.
Report includes Assessment, Signals checked, View reply links, measured values, rules and innocent explanations.
Patterns are not proof; normal users can trigger individual flags.

supporting_sources.title: Implementation and review discussion
key_facts: Scans up to 1000 posts; public implementation explains additive heuristics and limitations.
Automation signals do not establish AI authorship. Human behavior alone cannot produce strongest assessment.

prerequisites: Your own public Bluesky handle, or the author's example handle simonwillison.net; no login required for this check

steps.instruction: Open the [Bluesky reply bot checker](https://tools.simonwillison.net/bluesky-bot-check). Enter **simonwillison.net** as a practice example, or use your own public handle. Click **Check account**; do not enter a password or private messages.
Wait for **Assessment** to appear. Read the date range and number of scanned posts before interpreting the result: this is a sample, not the account's complete history.
Scroll to **Signals checked**. Choose one rule and read its measured value, threshold and **Innocent explanations**. Write down one reason a real person could trigger it.
Use a **View reply** link to inspect an example in context. Compare the actual exchange with the flag rather than treating a question mark or quick response as proof.

Finish with a narrow conclusion such as 'this rule flagged this pattern; authorship remains unknown.' Do not publish an accusation or report an account solely because of this score. If the lookup fails, retry later rather than interpreting missing data.
